title: When AI Never Stops, Should You?
coverage: expanded selected original paragraphs with speaker/header context; not full source
headings: L102 #### **From last week: [When AI Fakes, Can You Tell?](https://theslowai.substack.com/p/ai-fakes-and-truths)**

passages.text: - Try one simple question that asks the tool to hand you a single thought.
The invitation to your AI tool (at the end of a session, or when feeling too much noise):
> What one thought from this chat should I carry with me offline?
Then, when the tool gives you a line, do this:
> Breathe in, notice how the thought sits in your body, and take one slow step away from the screen.
> Let the answer percolate in your own mind, without asking the tool to add more.

If you cannot go outside, place a hand on something natural, a plant, a window ledge warmed by the sun, a cup of tea. The point is to move attention out of the continual loop of asking, and into a single, held moment.
This is not a ritual for performance.
It is a small practice that trains you to finish with care.
If you are new to Slow AI, our first invitation was, Teach It Something It Cannot Know.

At first the question felt abstract. But as I stayed with it, I noticed how silence and gaps gave the thought weight. Poetry, I realised, works because of what it leaves open, the pauses between lines, the unsaid that waits to be felt rather than explained.
- Try the same question at the start and end of a session, and note the difference.

If you would like to keep practising beyond this week’s prompt, you might like *A Gentle Guide to Reflection with AI* (pay what-you-wish). Think of it as a companion you can return to whenever you feel pulled too quickly back into the screen.
#### **From last week: When AI Fakes, Can You Tell?**
If you try this week’s prompt, I would love to see the single thought your tool offered, and to know whether you went outside and touched grass.
